summary: npm package hosts obfuscated Cloudflare-Turnstile phishing HTML, abusing registry as static CDN
details: The package consists of a single index.html file set as `main`. The HTML renders a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' Turnstile challenge page and contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript (string-array decoder functions `_0x3c31`/`_0x3bf2`, hex-indexed calls) that reconstructs a destination URL at runtime, concatenating a decoded prefix with the suffix 'dflare.com' to impersonate the real cloudflare.com domain. There are no lifecycle scripts (`preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall`/`prepare`), no JavaScript entry point, and because `main` points at HTML, `require()`/`import` of this package from Node cannot load or execute the obfuscated code. Installing this package does not run the payload on the installer's machine; the harm model is browser-side phishing of end users who fetch the HTML via an npm CDN proxy (unpkg/jsdelivr), using the registry as free static hosting for a Cloudflare-impersonation landing page.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
